$comment: Something someone does that costs them something and leaves the world different than it would have been. Both halves are load-bearing. If it costs nothing it is play or rest, not work. If the world would have gotten there anyway it is weather, not work — the theory calls the difference natural-history: what happens on its own, for free. Work is what you spend yourself to make happen instead. This is the plain sense and it is also the formal one: a work-act costs strictly more than nothing, and lands somewhere the world was not already headed.

name.$comment: What the work is called, as it is said: 'writing a report about the baseline of a micro-enterprise'.

to.$comment: The state it leaves behind. Must differ from what would have happened anyway — if it does not, nothing was done.

cost.$comment: What it spends that does not come back — attention, hours, goodwill, money. Strictly more than nothing: work recorded as free is play, rest, or weather wearing a work's name.

otherwise.$comment: What happens if nobody does it. Worth writing down where it is not obvious, because it is the only thing 'to' can be compared against — and comparing them is how you tell work from weather.

needs.$comment: What the doer must be able to do for that cost to be the real cost. More capability never makes the same work cost more, so a cost quoted without saying who could pay it is a cost nobody can reproduce.

$comment-absences: No worker: who does it belongs to the relation that assigns it — an office's deontic profile is where the doer enters. Naming the worker here would stop the work from being assignable to anyone else. No done key: whether it happened is something you check, not something the record claims about itself. No duration: cost is what does not come back, and time is one way of saying it, never the thing itself.
